content:
Ava Reynolds: WIP thought — I'm proposing we rewrite the admission shim to track "slot lineage" (stable slot IDs across evictions) so the allocator can reattach inflight KV state more safely.
Marco Chen: Can you outline the motivation? What does lineage buy us vs current lease IDs?
Ava Reynolds: Main goals: 1) reduce cold KV warming on preempt, 2) allow safe late-join re-attachment, 3) make eviction refunds less noisy. Need to balance metadata cost.
Priya Kapoor: Tradeoffs: persistent lineage means more metadata, GC, and we might need a central directory or gossip. That could hurt startup perf.
Ken O'Neill: How would this affect the admission surface? Any API churn for adapters?
Ava Reynolds: Minimal API changes imo. Sketch:
```
interface AdmissionShim {
  allocate(request): SlotToken  // includes slot_id, lineage_version
  attach(slot_id, lineage_version, kvhint): AttachResult
  release(slot_id)
}
```
Marco Chen: attach(...) returning AttachResult that says "reused" vs "fresh" is important for telemetry and scoring.
Priya Kapoor: Agreed. Also need a safe fallback when lineage info is lost — fall back to cold attach but mark for slower path.
runtime-bot: noted: add telemetry hooks: admission.attach.result, lineage.cache_hit_rate, lineage.eviction_reuse_pct
Ken O'Neill: What about security/isolation? stable slot IDs persisting across tenants could leak hints. needs per-tenant salt or opaque tokens.
Ava Reynolds: Per-tenant salt + ephemeral lineage epochs solves cross-tenant correlation. lineage_version should be opaque.
Marco Chen: Another cost: metadata churn for short-lived tiny requests. Maybe only enable lineage for lanes > N tokens or requests flagged "heavy".
Priya Kapoor: We could add heuristic: if expected_inflight_tokens > threshold -> request.mark_for_lineage 
Ava Reynolds: rollout plan idea: 1) implement shim behind flag; 2) enable lineage for high-latency tenants in canary; 3) measure warming reduction and KV reuse; 4) toggle on progressively.
Ken O'Neill: How to measure success? SLOs: p50 token latency, kv-warmup CPU delta, and cold-attach percent.
Ava Reynolds: Example KQ metric set:
- lineage.reuse_ratio
- kv.warmup_time_ms
- p50/p95 tail delta (canary vs control)
Marco Chen: Also watch for GC backlog and metadata DB ops/sec — if that spikes, revert.
Priya Kapoor: Implementation note: make lineage store sharded in-memory with async durable checkpoints to avoid sync DB on allocate.
Ava Reynolds: If we rely on async durability, we need strong reconcilers to avoid orphaned slot_ids. ops will want a cleanup job.
deploy-bot: ops-checklist created: lineage-orphan-sweeper job + alert lineage-db-latency>100ms
Ken O'Neill: One last thought — admission shim should expose a simple fastpath: allocate->attach where slot token contains enough to continue without coordinator in the common case.
Ava Reynolds: Yeah fastpath-first, fallback to coordinator for complex reattach.
Marco Chen: Thumbs up from me to prototype. @Priya can you pair on design doc section for GC/ops?
Priya Kapoor: yep, I'll draft GC and perf constraints this week. :+1:
Ken O'Neill: I'll follow on adapters and rollout gating.
Ava Reynolds: I'll open RFC follow-up PR with the interface and a prototype server. Thanks all :rocket:
deploy-bot: started canary pipeline for branch/slotlineage-proto — will post status updates
Marco Chen: Heard — please post perf numbers in #eng-runtime when available.
